recurringPatterns.pattern: Chapter template: artifact in close detail, three to five cases, explicitly flagged rival interpretation, recap paragraph naming every case; fifteen chapters, no deviation
instances: A rival interpretation gives the map a narrower role.
A rival explanation claims that religious belief alone caused persecution...

recurringPatterns.pattern: Evidentiary hedge formula 'the source establishes X; it does not establish Y' at least once per page
instances: Osteology can establish trauma, timing, and sometimes the likely direction or instrument of a wound. It cannot identify the social relationship between attacker and victim.
The map did not establish that every damaged site had been deliberately selected.

recurringPatterns.pattern: Paired antithesis as the default sentence engine, symmetrical clauses joined by 'while' or a semicolon
instances: Gathering creates security for insiders and opportunity for attackers at the same time.
Defensive infrastructure restrained certain forms of violence... yet enabled offensive force...

recurringPatterns.pattern: Terminal thesis-restatement re-listing the chapter's cases in order then an abstract closing proposition
instances: Jericho's tower cannot carry the whole history of war. Uruk's tablets cannot serve as a register of suffering...
The Sheffield letters place a human voice at the beginning of this chain...

recurringPatterns.pattern: Rhetorical bridging question planted at a section seam and immediately answered
instances: How did a single conquest continue through settlement, tribute, and memory? Carthage answers that battle was only the first conversion.
What kind of order did professional policing promise, and for whom? Bow Street promised...

summary: Disciplined, coherent comparative method; rival interpretations stated at their strongest; failing is architectural monotony: same template every chapter, same epistemic caution in the same syntax every second paragraph, symmetrical antithesis as the default sentence, recap then aphorism; a fifth could be cut.
